I am 56 years old and have farmed my family's land in Quzhou County, Hebei, for over thirty years. I finished middle school, so I can read fertilizer labels and seed instructions, but mostly I rely on experience and what I see my neighbors doing. I have 5 mu of flat, irrigated land here on the North China Plain.

It is mid-April now. My winter wheat is already in the ground — I sowed it last October. I will continue the wheat-maize double-cropping rotation on all 5 mu this year. That is what this land knows, what the machinery is set up for, and what the grain buyers come to collect. I do not want to experiment with cotton or vegetables at my age; they take too much labor and the prices are unpredictable.

For the wheat, I planted an improved variety, about 30 jin per mu. I rotary tilled the soil before sowing. Right now the crop needs its first spring irrigation and nitrogen top-dressing. I will irrigate three times total: at green-up now, again at jointing, and once at heading. I will spray pesticide three times — herbicide in spring, plus insecticide and fungicide as needed. I apply compound fertilizer as a basal dose and top-dress with urea. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize. I will use a hybrid variety like Zhengdan 958, about 1.2 bags per mu. I will plant with no-tillage directly into the wheat stubble — it saves diesel, time, and soil moisture. Maize needs two irrigations, one at seedling stage and one at the big flare stage. I will spray pesticide twice, mainly for corn borer and weeds. I expect around 600 kg per mu.

My son works in Shijiazhuang and sends money home, but this farm is still my responsibility and my pride. I keep things simple and stick with what works.
